cohort: Women with 22 weeks or more of gestation who underwent emergency obstetric hysterectomy during/immediately after delivery or within the puerperium at Aziz Fatima Teaching Hospital, Faisalabad, Pakistan between January 2012 and December 2016.
finding: The incidence of emergency obstetric hysterectomy was 0.25%, with the most common indication being life-threatening postpartum hemorrhage (47.5%), primarily caused by placenta previa (47.5%).
followup_time: Through the puerperium (variable, but typically 6-8 weeks postpartum)
